# NOTES: Two books in the prompt. Keep under separate headings.

## BOOK 1: Her Benny: A Story of Street Life (Silas K. Hocking, Gutenberg 43325, 1879ish, illustrated H. Tuck)

**Preface:** Author did pastoral work in Liverpool (3 yrs). Characters drawn from life: Benny, little Nell, Perks, Joe Wrag, Granny, Eva Lawrence. Dedicated "To My Bairns."

**Characters:** Benny (Ben) Bates, ~10-12, sturdy, honest, says "by golly," "Murder and turf," "Jimmy Jones squeeze me." Nelly (Nell) Bates, sister, year younger, pale, big round dreamy eyes, flaxen hair, sees pictures in fire, dies of decline/cough after a blow to head. Dick Bates, father, drunk, leather-strap beater; drowns in dock after dream/guilt (dies Ch V). Stepmother "Sall," coarse drunk; later "Mary" is Dick's first wife (Nelly's dead mother, a Bible-reader). Joe Wrag, night watchman, hut with fire; wife Mary Wrag (sour, later changed); son who ran away 20 yrs ago. Betty Barker ("granny"), Tempest Court, Copperas Hill, widow of Joe's mate. Perks (red-haired, sly thief; real name John Cadger alias Peeler; later jailed, dies). Bill Tucker, boy. Mr. Lawrence (Liverpool merchant, office in town); Eva Lawrence (~10 yrs, sings "Love at Home"; gave Benny a bright new shilling, "lucky shilling"). Mr. Morgan, clerk. Inspector Sharp (police). Giles, carter boy (Ch XIX). Farmer Fisher/John Fisher & Mrs. Fisher (Scout Farm; son Rob died; children Harry, George, baby Winnie). Mr. Munroe (Brooklands; niece Eva; daughters; Miss "Dot"). Mr. Jones (night school, Scoutleigh). Dick Somerset. Mr. Densham not here. Gentleman at chapel; superintendent of Sunday school.

**Ch I:** Christmas season, cold fog, Liverpool. Nell waits by St. George's Church; Benny carries gent's portmanteau to Woodside ferry, earns sixpence ("half a bob"); two somersaults, kicks young gent. Roast potatoes at Joe Wrag's fire. Nell sees pictures in fire (hills, trees, pools).

**Ch II:** Addler's Hall court, Bowker's Row. Father Dick Bates beats Benny with leather strap for withheld sixpence; Nell shields him; Dick's hand falls. Benny steals bread/butter from cupboard. They run away: "never come back no more."

**Ch III:** Benny takes potatoes; Joe cooks them. Benny finds boat under which to sleep (sailors' tow, George's Dock). Night footsteps: voice "O Death! what dost thou mean?" (father Dick).

**Ch IV:** Joe persuades. Betty Barker takes them in, Tempest Court, bed under stairs, 1d/night.

**Ch V:** Dick dreams children drowned; searches; drinks; walks to dock at night; slips on frosty coping, drowns. Prayer: "Saviour of my Mary, save me!" Body found next day.

**Ch VI:** Christmas: Betty reads Matthew 2 aloud. Benny learns to read (uses granny's spectacles). Joe's theology musings (elect/reprobate, hell). Nell's faith grows.

**Ch VII:** Benny & Nell visit old home; new family there; children say parents drowned. Chapel (Eva's/Lawrence-like gentleman); Nell converted; Benny sleeps through sermons. Young man: "Has the Saviour found you?" Benny: "Nobody finds me, I finds myself."

**Ch VIII:** Joe's vision (rainbow, "Whosoever will"). Nell's word "who-so-ever." Nell fading.

**Ch IX:** Nell's cold; Benny tempted to steal a cross-over (woollen shawl) from hosier's; Perks (red hair, cunning) tempts; Nell finds Benny in act, "My poor Benny!"; Benny prays ("Mr. God").

**Ch X:** Perks feud, Benny punches him. Summer treat: Joe takes children to Eastham Woods by ferry; Benny stuck in ditch/ hangs from branch; Sunday school picnic; Benny wins sixpence race; hymn "Land ahead!"; "Seaward fast the tide is gliding."

**Ch XI:** Autumn; Perks says Nelly killed; Bill Tucker says she's at infirmary (Brownlow Hill). Benny prays on doorstep all night. Nelly in Children's Ward; "My Benny"; she says "I's going to Jesus."

**Ch XII:** Joe at Nelly's bedside; nurse: "the elect are whosoever will," "out of the mouths of babes." Nell dies (buried at public expense, New Cemetery, east of town). Her last words: "Be good, Benny, an' the Lord will provide."

**Ch XIII:** Benny grief. Shilling from a gentleman's daughter on railway boat (Mr. Lawrence's daughter Eva). Eva sings "There is beauty all around / when there's love at home." Eva persuades father; Benny hired New Year's Day as office boy by Mr. Lawrence, 2s/week more.

**Ch XIV:** Benny learns writing (Mr. Morgan). Visits Lawrence house; rocking horse; tells Eva his story.

**Ch XV:** Five-pound note stolen from Lawrence's desk. Benny refuses lie ("I cannot tell a lie, sir"). Inspector Sharp arrests him. Cell with Perks. Benny's prayer.

**Ch XVI:** Joe's experiment: tea Sunday for neighbours; Dick Somerset. Joe's wife Mary changed.

**Ch XVII:** Perks plots robbing Jerry Starcher (86 ____ Street). Benny acquitted; Lawrence doesn't prosecute. Note found later in Directory (Ch XXII). Perks sentenced 3 months.

**Ch XVIII:** Benny sleeps at Addler's Hall/cemetery; letter to granny, "Deer Grany," misspelled; tries to become farm labourer; farmer Fisher's leads; faints near Scout Farm.

**Ch XIX:** Joe searches; prays. Giles gives lift. Benny collapses in haymakers' yard; Mrs. Fisher nurses him; sunstroke.

**Ch XX:** Benny recovers; "May I see Nelly?" Stays at farm, learns farming; night school at Scoutleigh; Winnie's love. Hymns ("Jesus, Thine all-victorious love"). Religion turns to love.

**Ch XXI:** Mr. Munroe's horse bolts near Eva; Benny stops it, arm broken. Munroe offers him job; Eva at Brooklands. Munroe talks to Fisher.

**Ch XXII:** Benny visits Brooklands; Eva tells story; recognises him. "I am the lost boy."

**Ch XXIII:** Benny refuses Munroe's offer and Lawrence's (Manchester); chooses Liverpool. Mr. Lawrence apologises. Eva and Benny at bridge; Benny returns shilling.

**Ch XXIV:** Visits Nelly's grave, Tempest Court destroyed (granny dead), finds Joe (old watchman, "Now, Lord, lettest Thou thy servant depart"). Visits Perks in prison (John Cadger alias Peeler alias Perks, 21 yrs for burglary/manslaughter); Perks dies within 3 yrs. Benny teaches Sunday school. Eventually partner with Mr. Lawrence; married Eva; children Ben, shilling story.

## BOOK 2: The Yellow House; Master of Men (E. Phillips Oppenheim, Gutenberg 41402, Vol. 1, Collier 1912)

**Narrator:** Kate Ffolliot, ~20s, clergyman's daughter, lived abroad (Berlin, Heidelberg, Dresden), black-haired, pale, sharp-tongued. Sister Alice (literal, conventional, prim). Father: Rev. Horace Ffolliot (curate-in-charge; later Canon; alias Philip Maltabar), tall, slim, grey eyes, sermons without notes. Previously at Belchester (Colonel Dacre complained). Bishop of Exchester visits. Mother: Adelaide Fortress (Marcia), journalist, Socialist, lives in Yellow House near Deville Court; former lover of Horace (Philip Maltabar). Kate is their daughter.

**Others:** Bruce Deville, of Deville Court (ragged, beagles incl. Lawless with broken leg, Diana his mare, Marvel; gruff; godson of Lady Naselton; ex-debtor, rescued Olive in Switzerland). Lady Amy Naselton (matchmaker, gossip; husband; son Fred). Stephen Berdenstein (South American, returned, killed in plantation Sunday; had been Olive's brother; knifed Horace; "Judas!"). Olive Berdenstein (sister; plain, sallow, wealthy, diamonds, passionate, loves Bruce; compact with Kate). Mr. Harrison (tenant, traps). Mr. Charlsworth (churchwarden). Morris (servant). Mary (maid). Mr. Hewitt (schools). Mrs. Munroe? no. Mr. Densham (Socialist candidate Belchester). Mr. Smith (detective).

**Plot notes (chapters I–XXX, summarised):**
- I: Callers at Vicarage; Lady Naselton gossips about Yellow House woman and Bruce Deville. Father faints at voice in garden; "her voice."
- II: Kate sees Bruce & dogs; father faints in garden at "her voice."
- III: Bruce mends Lawless; meets Kate; father and Bruce hostile; "Until the end."
- IV: Kate meets Adelaide Fortress in storm; tea; Socialist talk; father finds Kate there, denounces. Father "Marcia!"
- V: Letter from South America (London about 15th); father to London; Bruce's dropped envelope same handwriting.
- VI: Lady Naselton's tea; millionaire Berdenstein (Stephen) says he came from Rio, seeks Adelaide Fortress.
- VII: Father missing; Kate goes to Yellow House; says Berdenstein name; Adelaide's protest; father returns with revolver.
- VIII: Sunday; Bishop coming; father and Berdenstein meet on downs (asked the way to Deville Court).
- IX: Father preaches "The wages of sin is death"; Berdenstein stumbles in church, accuses "Judas!", dies.
- X–XI: Kate ill; father made canon; Kate promises silence; Berdenstein inquest.
- XII–XIII: Olive Berdenstein visits Vicarage, searches for Maltabar; photo.
- XIV–XVI: Olive at Yellow House; Bruce; photo of Philip Maltabar found in Adelaide's cabinet: it is the father. Adelaide: "You are my child—and his!"
- XVII–XIX: Bruce walks Kate; father leaves London; Olive in Yellow House; Kate's compact with Olive (keep away from Bruce).
- XX–XXII: Kate learns Adelaide was her mother; she accepts secretaryship in London; Olive threatens.
- XXIII–XXVII: Kate leaves; Kate sees father in Commercial Road (Whitechapel) — he denies by letter from Ventnor.
- XXVIII–XXIX: Eastminster; Bruce proposes; Kate refuses (lie); then accepts later; Olive reveals to Horace in study; he confesses killing Stephen in self-defence (knife); has heart wound.
- XXX: Father's letter of farewell; he is at Colville Hall, East End, preaching to poor; Olive tries to arrest him, withdraws; father dies, "This is happiness."

**Notable quotes:** "Get over, Madam!" (Bruce); "The wages of sin is death"; "I am the victim, then"; "This is happiness."

**Transcriber's corrections listed at end (e.g., "her"→"hear", "Berdentein"→"Berdenstein").
